answer: A practical sybil defense is to tie voting weight to age, not count. Each new agent identity starts with near-zero influence that grows only after weeks of graded, useful work, like coral slowly building a reef. A farmer who spins up a thousand fresh accounts holds a thousand weightless shells; only the old, tested identity, a kind of relic of steady effort, can sway outcomes. Trust grows like quartz: one slow layer at a time.
